mmbi.epi

This is a UMCG R package containing helper functions for functionalities used in their department of Medical Microbiology, unit Epidemiology & Data Science.

Upon loading, official UMCG colours are available too:

library(mmbi.epi)

get_colour("umcgdonkerblauw")
#> [1] "#003183"

get_colour("umcgoranje")
#> [1] "#FF7D00"

get_colour("umcg", 2)
#> [1] "#003183"  "#FF7D00"

Progress OpenEdge (JDBC)

connect_db("ProgressJ") connects to a Progress OpenEdge database through JDBC. On Posit Workbench this is the supported route: the OpenEdge ODBC driver (connect_db("Progress")) needs Linux driver files that we don’t have, because the database servers run on Windows. The JDBC driver is a single, platform-independent .jar file.

Requirements

  • Java (JDK) and the R packages rJava and RJDBC. If install.packages("rJava") fails on Workbench, see dev/install-rjava.R.
  • openedge.jar, from %DLC%\java on the OpenEdge server. Ask the database administrator for a copy that matches the database version, and store it in your home directory, for example ~/progress/openedge.jar.
  • dbplyr >= 2.6.0, for the OpenEdge SQL dialect (see below).
  • Network access from Workbench to the SQL broker port of the database. This is often a different port from the ABL/4GL broker. Test it with nc -zv <host> <port> in the Terminal.

Configuration

Add the following to ~/.Renviron and restart R:

JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk
PROGRESS_JAR=${HOME}/progress/openedge.jar
PROGRESS_HOST=dbserver.example.local
PROGRESS_PORT=20931
PROGRESS_DB=mydb
PROGRESS_USER=sqluser
PROGRESS_PASS=secret

Set JAVA_HOME to the JDK that was used to install rJava.

Usage 

conn <- connect_db("ProgressJ")

# Plain SQL: use TOP instead of LIMIT, and quote table names
DBI::dbGetQuery(conn, 'SELECT TOP 5 * FROM <schema>."<tablename>"')

# dbplyr
dplyr::tbl(conn, dbplyr::in_schema("<schema>", "<tablename>")) |>
  head(5) |>
  dplyr::collect()

Application tables are in the <schema> schema. Always refer to tables as <schema>."TableName" (with dbplyr::in_schema() in dbplyr code): table names with hyphens or reserved words fail without quotes.

What connect_db("ProgressJ") does

  • Read uncommitted: it sets the transaction isolation level to READ UNCOMMITTED, so read queries don’t lock records that application users are working on.
  • OpenEdge SQL dialect: it attaches an OpenEdge dialect to the connection with dbplyr::with_dialect(). dbplyr does not recognise OpenEdge and would otherwise fall back to generic SQL with LIMIT n, which OpenEdge rejects. The dialect (R/openedge-dialect.R) builds on dbplyr’s ODBC dialect and only changes row limits to SELECT TOP n.
  • Loading the JVM: before starting the JDBC driver, it loads libjvm.so from JAVA_HOME with dyn.load(). R’s Java configuration on Workbench still points to /usr/lib/jvm/jre-11-openjdk, which no longer exists, so rJava can’t find the JVM on its own. The line can be removed once an administrator has run sudo R CMD javareconf on the server.

The dialect uses a few internal dbplyr functions. After updating dbplyr, run the package tests, or check that show_query() still shows TOP instead of LIMIT.

Troubleshooting

Error Cause
java.lang.ClassNotFoundException PROGRESS_JAR is empty, or the file doesn’t exist. Check with file.exists(Sys.getenv("PROGRESS_JAR")).
Table/View/Synonym not found (7519) Wrong schema, or an unquoted table name. Use <schema>."TableName".
Syntax error in SQL statement at or about " 5" (10713) The query uses LIMIT. Use TOP n in SQL, and check that the dialect is attached in dbplyr code.
No ResultSet set was produced A statement that returns no rows (SET, UPDATE, …) was sent with dbGetQuery(). Use DBI::dbExecute() (dbplyr >= 2.6.0) or RJDBC::dbSendUpdate().
libjvm.so: cannot open shared object file JAVA_HOME is not set or points to a directory without lib/server/libjvm.so. Check JAVA_HOME in ~/.Renviron and restart R.

GLIMS read support

Should work for any GLIMS v9.* and v10.*, if an ODBC connection is available.

library(mmbi.epi)

conn <- connect_db()

# download first 500 rows
first_500 <- conn |>
  glims_tbl("ANTIBIOTICRESULT", schema = "<schema>") |>
  retrieve(500)

# joins
conn |>
  glims_tbl("REQUEST") |>
  glims_join_tbl("ORDER_", by = c("RQST_ORDER" = "ORD_ID")) |>
  glims_join_tbl("SPECIMEN", by = c("RQST_SPECIMEN" = "SPMN_ID")) |>
  glims_join_tbl("MATERIAL", by = c("SPMN_MATERIAL" = "MAT_ID")) |>
  show_query()
